stemMd: Why does conversion of pyruvate to lactate help sustain glycolysis when oxygen supply is inadequate?

options.label: B
options.textMd: It removes the need for glucose.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It directly supplies the entire aerobic ATP yield.

explanationMd: Glycolysis needs NAD+ to accept electrons. Reducing pyruvate to lactate oxidises NADH back to NAD+, allowing glycolysis to continue. The benefit is cofactor recycling, not a large extra ATP yield.

distractorRationale.e: Lactate formation does not release oxygen.
distractorRationale.d: Nucleic-acid synthesis is unrelated to this redox step.
distractorRationale.c: Fermentation does not reproduce oxidative phosphorylation.
distractorRationale.b: Glycolysis still consumes a carbon substrate.
